en.title: Cliff Booth's Trailer Hits Theaters Ahead of Netflix Debut
en.summary: Fans can finally catch the first official trailer for Quentin Tarantino and David Fincher's 'The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth'. The highly anticipated Netflix film's trailer is currently playing exclusively in select theaters.
en.body:
Get ready to head back to the world of 1960s Hollywood, as the first official trailer for **David Fincher** and **Quentin Tarantino**'s **The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth** has officially landed. In a move that feels perfectly suited to the duo's cinematic sensibilities, the trailer isn't just dropping online; it's currently playing exclusively in theaters worldwide. This is your chance to see **Brad Pitt** reprise his iconic role as the effortlessly cool stuntman before the film's global Netflix premiere.

The trailer's theatrical debut is attached to showings of the new **Resident Evil** movie, a partnership that's generating significant buzz among cinephiles. For those who might not be rushing to the cinema for a horror flick, fear not. The online debut is slated for Monday, September 21st, offering a wider audience a glimpse of what's to come. This follows a brief, accidental leak last weekend, which Netflix swiftly addressed, underscoring the studio's tight control over the film's rollout. The secrecy surrounding **The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth** has been intense, making this trailer a crucial moment for fans eager for more details about this highly anticipated **Once Upon a Time in Hollywood** spin-off.

## A Glimpse from the Big Screen
The unusual choice to premiere the trailer in cinemas was first hinted at by the film's own cast members. Social media has been abuzz with leaked images and discussions, with actors from the movie sharing snippets and confirming the trailer's theatrical placement. This direct connection from the set to the audience adds an extra layer of excitement and intimacy to the promotion. It’s a bold strategy from Netflix, positioning **The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth** as one of their biggest original film releases for 2026, aiming to capture the big-screen magic even for its preview content. The film promises to delve deeper into the life of Cliff Booth, a character who captured audiences' imaginations in Tarantino's 2019 masterpiece.

## What Fans Are Saying
For dedicated fans of **Quentin Tarantino** and **David Fincher**, this trailer's release is a monumental event. The anticipation for any new project from these visionary directors is always sky-high, and a spin-off centered on a beloved character like Cliff Booth is particularly exciting. The decision to play the trailer in theaters alongside a major release like **Resident Evil** speaks volumes about Netflix's confidence in the film's potential to be a significant cultural moment. Discussions online are already dissecting every frame, speculating about the narrative arcs and the return of **Brad Pitt**'s character. The exclusivity of the theatrical trailer suggests a desire to recapture some of the shared cinematic experience that often gets lost in the streaming era, making the wait for the online debut all the more tantalizing.

## What's Next
Mark your calendars: the global online debut of **The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth** trailer is set for Monday, September 21st. The film itself is slated for release in 2026, with further details on its specific premiere date on Netflix expected soon, following its IMAX debut on November 25, 2026, and Netflix debut on December 23, 2026.

content_raw: Picture Credits: Netflix If you’re heading out to the movies this weekend, make sure you get to your seat before the previews start. The first official trailer for David Fincher and Quentin Tarantino’s highly anticipated Netflix movie, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , is currently playing exclusively in theaters (following an accidental leak last weekend). As we approach the holiday season, Netflix is revving up the promotional engine for what is undeniably their biggest original film of 2026. The Once Upon a Time in Hollywood spin-off has been heavily shrouded in secrecy, but fans are finally getting their first real glimpse of Brad Pitt’s return as the iconic stuntman following the teaser that dropped during the Super Bowl at the top of the year. Currently, the only way to see the trailer in high definition is on the big screen. Netflix has attached the teaser exclusively to screenings of the new Resident Evil movie in cinemas worldwide. If you don’t feel like buying a movie ticket just to catch a two-minute preview, you won’t have to wait long; we’ve learned the  global online debut is on Monday, September 21st . That comes a week after the trailer leaked online , but Netflix quickly swatted down most of what was published online.  Netflix declined to comment on the trailer’s release date or some of the other promotional cadence dates when we reached out.  How do we know it’s in theaters? The cast told us! Word of the trailer’s theatrical placement actually comes straight from the stars of the movie themselves. Over on Instagram, social media was buzzing with leaked images from the trailer. But a closer look at the accounts sharing the footage reveals a fun connection: they are actors in the film! Actor Zedrick Restauro posted a photo from inside a movie theater, writing, “If you’re seeing Resident Evil make sure you’re early enough for the trailers to see @jaybeetadena @mattgr00ve in new Cliff Booth trailer.” Actor Matt Groove (who is part of the movie’s massive ensemble cast) then reshared the post to his own Instagram story, confirming the news alongside fellow cast member JB Tadena . Groove also shared a few blurry, bootlegged snaps of the trailer (thanking user @ohmeigawd for the footage), giving fans a sneak peek at Pitt back in action and a look at Groove and Tadena’s characters cruising in a car. Others have also seen the new trailer in theaters and posted bootleg copies online. The hype train doesn’t stop at the trailer. While David Fincher ( The Social Network , Mindhunter ) is sitting in the director’s chair for the film, Quentin Tarantino is still heavily involved—and he’s expanding the cinematic universe onto the written page. It was just announced that Tarantino has written a brand new tie-in novel based on the character, set to arrive just before Fincher’s film hits Netflix. Titled The Adventures of Cliff Boo
